paper.title_en: Impact of Primordial Magnetic Field-induced Small-scale Power on Non-linear Structure Formation and Cosmic Reionization
paper.abstract_en: Primordial magnetic fields (PMFs) can enhance small-scale matter perturbations and alter halo formation and reionization. We evolve PMF-modified initial spectra with collisionless $N$-body simulations and use the halo catalogues as sources for semi-numerical ionization and 21-cm brightness-temperature fields in the saturated spin-temperature limit. We compare $Λ$CDM with four PMF models, $B_0=100$, $130$, $150$, and $170\,\mathrm{pG}$, at $n_B=-2.9$. With cosmology and source prescriptions fixed, the PMF models show enhanced small-scale clustering, more early low-mass haloes and earlier reionization. Their volume-averaged reionization midpoints advance by $Δz_{50}\simeq0.50$--$2.14$, with changes in ionization morphology and 21-cm power spectra. The Thomson optical depth rises from $τ_{\rm e}\simeq0.0547$ for $Λ$CDM to $0.0595$--$0.0786$. These simulation-relative offsets span $0.66$--$3.28$ times the Planck 2018 uncertainty, $σ_τ=0.0073$, and are not exclusion significances. The common source efficiency $N_{\rm ion}$ is calibrated to a reference history approaching ionization completion near $z\sim6$ and an optical depth close to Planck 2018, without model-specific retuning. We omit subsequent magnetic-field evolution and dissipative magnetic heating. Observational bounds require joint treatment of astrophysical degeneracies and numerical uncertainties.
